_meta.description: Suburban-SOC unified security index. Pins ECS fields to keyword/ip/date so cross-index aggregations and dashboards are consistent (fixes the dynamic text+keyword drift that silently failed shard aggregations). WS0.3: tenant.id is a first-class keyword. WS0.5: backed by a per-tenant data stream (logstash-security-<tenant>) under ILM policy logstash-security-ilm. #249/#250: command-line/script-block-shaped fields (process.args, *CommandLine, *ScriptBlockText, *uri — explicit properties plus the long_command_fields dynamic_template) use a lowercase normalizer (so Sigma's lowercase literals match mixed-case real telemetry via wildcard-query normalization) and a raised ignore_above so long values, e.g. encoded PowerShell, aren't silently dropped from the index. #263: process.args/process.parent.args/winlog.event_data.ScriptBlockText/winlog.event_data.ImagePath (and the long_command_fields dynamic_template backing any future field of the same shape) are raised further to ignore_above:32766 — 8191 (#249/#250's original raise from the default 1024) was still below real PowerShell 4104 chunk sizes (~20000 chars) and encoded-command-line lengths, letting both PowerShell Sigma rules and system_win_suspicious_service_binpath_lolbin.yml be silently bypassed by payload length. Note ignore_above:32766 is a CHARACTER ceiling, not the Lucene per-term 32766-BYTE hard limit it's numerically equal to — multi-byte UTF-8 content can exceed the byte limit while under the char ceiling, which would otherwise reject the whole document rather than just dropping the field (confirmed live during #263's review); configs/logstash.conf's ruby filter clamps byte-oversized values before they reach Elasticsearch to prevent that, tagging pipeline.byte_clamped separately from pipeline.truncated. Aggregations/sorts on these fields return the lowercased form; _source keeps original casing for Discover/evidence (except the rare byte-clamped case, where _source itself is clamped too — no way to preserve full fidelity there without risking the same document-rejection failure). #290: the 5 new Zeek-derived ECS fields #228 introduced never got long_command_fields' lowercase_normalizer/raised-ignore_above treatment, falling through to strings_as_keyword (case-sensitive, ignore_above:1024) instead — tests/detections/sigma_eval.py matches case-insensitively by default (mirroring real Sigma semantics) but production Elasticsearch does not for an unnormalized keyword field, so a single uppercase char anywhere in real telemetry silently evades net_zeek_dns_crypto_mining_pool.yml/net_zeek_dns_doh_non_standard.yml (query|endswith) and net_zeek_http_cobalt_strike_beacon.yml (uri|contains) while the fixture test stays green. Fixed with explicit properties (dns.question.name, tls.validation_status, zeek.http.host, url.path) rather than extending long_command_fields' path_match glob — path_match matches the FULL dotted path, so the existing `*uri`/`*url` patterns never actually matched `url.path` (the path doesn't END in "url"), which is exactly why it silently fell through despite looking covered; explicit properties sidestep that ambiguity entirely and match this file's own established convention for every other case-normalized field. url.path alone gets ignore_above:32766 (not 8191, unlike its 3 siblings) — it had NO explicit ignore_above at all before this fix (falling to the default 1024), confirming #290's own suspicion that the uri->url.path rename (#228) silently dropped ignore_above coverage; 32766 matches the payload-length intent the pre-existing `*uri`/`*url` long_command_fields patterns were meant to provide (C2 beacon URIs/exfil query strings, same bypass shape #263 fixed for PowerShell). user_agent.original (also named in #290) deliberately excluded: unlike the other 4, no producer renames or maps it anywhere in this pipeline today (suburban-soc-ecs.yml's own comment: field mapping "deliberately omitted... no rule selects on it yet") — normalizing a field nothing populates would be speculative, not a real fix; whoever adds it later must ALSO rename configs/logstash.conf's Category 0 bare user_agent string to user_agent.original in the same commit, or Zeek http.log's unrenamed string collides with the object mapping and drops every zeek.http document (same collision class already handled for zeek/version/the :5514 user_agent path). Security-auditor follow-up review of this same fix found and closed 2 more gaps: url.path's new ignore_above:32766 was not added to configs/logstash.conf's #263 byte-clamp long_fields hash, live-confirmed to reintroduce whole-document Lucene immense-term rejection on a fully attacker-controlled field (HTTP URI) — fixed by adding it there, plus a new CI-enforced CeilingConsistencyTests check that WALKS this template for every field at ignore_above:32766 and asserts each has a matching clamp entry, so a future field raised to this ceiling cannot skip it silently. And tls.client.server_name — same #228 batch, same case-sensitive hostname shape, with both a producer (configs/logstash.conf) and a live dashboard consumer (network_dashboard_v3.ndjson's SNI panel) — got the identical lowercase_normalizer/ignore_above:8191 treatment as its tls.validation_status sibling. ignore_above:8191 (used for every field here except url.path) is not an arbitrary convention: 8191×4=32764 is the largest character ceiling that stays under Lucene's 32766-BYTE hard limit for arbitrary UTF-8 even after lowercase_normalizer's case-folding growth (a handful of code points, e.g. U+0130, grow when case-folded) — 32766 requires the logstash.conf byte-clamp entry above; 8191 does not. OPERATIONAL NOTE: this is a data-stream-backed index template (see data_stream above) — like every prior ignore_above/normalizer change to this file (#249/#250, #263), it only shapes indices created AFTER it is applied; an operator must roll over each logstash-security-<tenant> data stream (POST <data-stream-name>/_rollover) for it to take effect on the currently-active write index, the same manual step #263 documented performing against the running production stack. #292: dns.answers (the new TXT-record-download-direction field) got an explicit ignore_above:8191 property rather than falling to strings_as_keyword's default 1024 — security-auditor review: unlike dns.question.name, which a 253-byte DNS-name protocol limit makes structurally unable to reach even the DEFAULT 1024 ceiling, a Zeek dns.log answers array element has no such bound, so the field this fix's own net_zeek_dns_txt_answer_abuse.yml rule selects on could be silently unindexed past 1024 chars — a query that can never find the value, not a crash, and with no pipeline.truncated tag either (dns.answers is deliberately NOT in configs/logstash.conf's long_fields byte-clamp hash, matching every other 8191-ceiling field here). Deliberately NO lowercase_normalizer: the rule's own answers|re pattern already spans both cases in its character class, so normalizing would only cost case-folding byte growth for no matching benefit. WARNING for a future raise to ignore_above:32766: configs/logstash.conf's byte-clamp ruby filter only clamps String values (`next unless val.is_a?(String)`) — dns.answers is a Zeek Array, so a long_fields entry for it would satisfy CeilingConsistencyTests' CI gate while the clamp itself silently no-ops, reintroducing the #263 whole-document rejection bug with CI green. Do not raise past 8191 without first making the clamp array-aware. #288: percent_lost/gaps/acks/ts_delta (Zeek capture_loss.log, bare unrenamed field names, no configs/logstash.conf entry maps them) got explicit numeric properties for the same reason every other explicit property in this file exists — index.mapping.ignore_malformed is true and the two dynamic_templates below only match_mapping_type:string, so a bare numeric field falls to Elasticsearch's own default dynamic type inference entirely, decided by whichever document happens to create the field first. percent_lost's steady-state healthy value is exactly 0 (an integer-shaped JSON number), so the very first capture_loss doc in a fresh backing index is the SAME shape as a #275-class false-healthy trap: if that first doc pins the field as a long, every later fractional value (3.7, 12.5 — the values scripts/setup/ai_agent/slo_metrics.py's capture_loss_max_pct metric actually needs to see) is silently ignore_malformed-dropped from the index while remaining in _source, so the metric reads a permanent, healthy-looking 0.0 while the sensor is actually dropping packets. Pinned to float explicitly so the type is never left to chance on rollover (data streams re-derive dynamic mappings from the template independently on each new backing index). #337: user.name/related.user were mapped keyword with NO ignore_above at all - unlike every other field in this file, which falls to strings_as_keyword's default 1024 the moment it's unmapped, an explicit keyword property with no ignore_above gets Elasticsearch's own default (2147483647, effectively unbounded), so a long value isn't ignore_above-dropped at all - it reaches Lucene directly, the same #263/#290/#344 whole-document immense-term rejection path, just with no char-ceiling backstop to catch it first. user.name (Sysmon's User field, renamed by #328's fix to the ECS-correct [user][name] nested shape, single-valued) raised to ignore_above:32766 (matching this file's convention for genuinely attacker-controlled fields) - configs/logstash.conf's byte-clamp long_fields hash was updated in the same fix, required by this file's own CeilingConsistencyTests CI gate. related.user is DIFFERENT: security-auditor review of the first draft caught that ECS defines related.* as an ARRAY field, and this file's own dns.answers precedent already documents why that matters - configs/logstash.conf's byte-clamp filter only clamps String values (next unless val.is_a?(String)), so raising an array field to 32766 would satisfy CeilingConsistencyTests' CI gate (the entry exists) while the clamp itself silently no-ops the moment a real producer populates it, reintroducing the exact whole-document-rejection bug on an unclamped array element - the same do-not-raise-past-8191-without-first-making-the-clamp-array-aware rule dns.answers already states. Mapped ignore_above:8191 instead, matching its related.hosts sibling (same array shape, needs no clamp - 8191*4=32764 stays under Lucene's 32766-byte limit even for all-multi-byte content). No producer for it in configs/logstash.conf today either way (grep-confirmed) - pre-emptive hardening, not a live gap. Separately, the truncation-tagging filter (configs/logstash.conf's #252 ruby block) previously modeled a single global ceiling for every field it tracked; #337 also restructured it to a per-field ceiling so the 6 OTHER Sysmon-rename-produced fields at their own real (lower) ignore_above values - process.executable/process.parent.name (8191, explicit below) and file.path/user.target.name/process.pe.original_file_name/file.hash.sha256 (1024, via strings_as_keyword, no explicit property needed) - are now measurably tagged pipeline.truncated too, closing a visibility gap #252's own stated purpose (make silent ignore_above drops measurable) never actually covered for them. #442: added process.pid/process.parent.pid (long — always integers, ECS-canonical type, no fractional-value trap like percent_lost's) and user.id (keyword — ECS defines user.id as keyword, not long, since it also has to hold non-numeric identifiers like Windows SIDs on other sources; auditd's own auid/uid values are just a short numeric string in that field) for the new configs/logstash.conf auditd SYSCALL+EXECVE correlation branch (#441's Linux execve telemetry prerequisite). All three previously fell to Elasticsearch's own default dynamic type inference — the exact 'decided by whichever document happens to create the field first' risk #288 pinned percent_lost/gaps/acks/ts_delta against, even though (unlike percent_lost) none of these three has a fractional-vs-integer split risk. user.id also got an explicit ignore_above:1024 rather than being left implicit — #337's own finding above is that an explicit keyword property with NO ignore_above gets Elasticsearch's unbounded default (2147483647), not strings_as_keyword's 1024; pinned to 1024 deliberately instead of by omission, even though auid/uid values are always short and not attacker-controlled the way user.name can be. process.executable/process.args/user.name needed no new mapping — already covered by the existing Sysmon-producer properties above, and configs/logstash.conf's long_fields byte-clamp hash already carries [process][args] and [user][name] entries from #263/#337, so no new CeilingConsistencyTests entry was needed either. #441 Part B: added source.bytes and destination.bytes (both long), needed by net_zeek_conn_outbound_volume_asymmetry's threshold companion. source.bytes had been a live field since #228 (orig_bytes rename, net_zeek_conn_icmp_tunnel_large.yml) with no explicit property at all — the same #288-class dynamic-type-inference risk this file's own history keeps closing, left unnoticed until a second numeric field (destination.bytes, the resp_bytes rename this same fix adds) needed pinning right next to it. Pinning both together rather than leaving the pre-existing one as a known-but-unfixed gap. #443/#444 (M23): added rule.name/rule.id/rule.category (all keyword, ignore_above:1024) for configs/logstash.conf's new Suricata eve.json alert.* mapping — the #337 lesson applies here too (an explicit keyword property with no ignore_above gets Elasticsearch's unbounded default, not strings_as_keyword's 1024), so all three are pinned deliberately rather than left implicit, same as user.id was. rule.id (Suricata's numeric signature_id) is mapped keyword, not a numeric type, matching ECS's own rule.id convention — some sources use non-numeric rule identifiers, and nothing in this pipeline queries it as a range/aggregation target the way process.pid or source.bytes are. None of the three needed a raised ignore_above:32766 or a matching configs/logstash.conf byte-clamp entry: rule content (a signature's own msg/category/SID) is authored by the ruleset maintainer, not attacker-controlled traffic content, the same reasoning that kept process.executable/process.parent.name at 8191 rather than 32766. threat.technique.id needed no new mapping — already covered by strings_as_keyword's dynamic fallback, the same fields the Zeek Intel-match branch already populates elsewhere in this pipeline. NOT live-verified against a real Suricata-produced eve.json document in the environment this was authored in — same disclosed gap as #442's own additions above.
